recognize_zh: 這不是電泳膠片，而是 Bio-Rad 高效液相層析（HPLC）的色譜圖：主峰為約 2.3 分鐘的 HbA0，約 3.6 分鐘處有明顯的陰影 HbA2 峰，標題說明為 HbA2 升高，提示 β 地中海型貧血帶因者；百分比數字在此圖解析度下無法判讀。
features: Cation-exchange HPLC chromatogram (Bio-Rad system) with absorbance versus retention time (0-6 min)
Dominant off-scale HbA0 peak at approximately 2.3 min
Shaded HbA2 peak at approximately 3.6 min, visually prominent relative to baseline
Small early-eluting peaks (approximately 1.1-1.8 min) corresponding to HbF, P2/P3, and glycated fractions
No abnormal variant peak (e.g., HbS or HbC window) is evident; peak percentage table is not shown
describe_en: The figure shows a cation-exchange high-performance liquid chromatography (HPLC) tracing rather than a conventional electrophoresis gel. There is a dominant HbA0 peak at approximately 2.3 minutes, small early-eluting minor fractions, and a shaded HbA2 peak at approximately 3.6 minutes. No abnormal variant peaks are identified in the S or C windows, and the numeric peak table is not included, so the HbA2 percentage cannot be verified from the image. Per the submitted history of increased HbA2 (typically >3.5%), findings are consistent with beta-thalassemia trait, to be correlated with red cell indices and iron status.

ddx.vs: Iron deficiency lowers HbA2 and can mask beta-thalassemia trait, so HbA2 should be interpreted with ferritin; it does not raise HbA2.
Alpha-thalassemia trait has normal or low HbA2 on HPLC and requires DNA testing for confirmation.

ddx.dx: HbE or Hb Lepore co-eluting in the A2 window
ddx.vs: HbE co-elutes with HbA2 on many HPLC systems giving a falsely very high A2 (typically >10%), distinguished by capillary electrophoresis or DNA analysis.
Delta-beta thalassemia shows markedly increased HbF with normal or low HbA2, unlike an isolated HbA2 elevation.
